import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 281

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/281](https://www.erdosproblems.com/281)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathematique (1980).
- [DaEr36] Davenport, H. and Erdős, P., *On sequences of positive integers*. Acta
  Arithmetica (1936), 147-151.
- [HaRo66] Halberstam, H. and Roth, K. F., *Sequences. Vol. I*. (1966), xx+291.
-/

open Filter Topology

namespace Erdos281

/-- Choices of congruence classes $a_i \pmod{n_i}$. -/
def ResidueChoice (n : ℕ → ℕ) := ∀ i : ℕ, ZMod (n i)

/-- The integers avoiding all congruences $a_i \pmod{n_i}$. -/
def avoidAll (n : ℕ → ℕ) (a : ResidueChoice n) : Set ℤ :=
  {m | ∀ i : ℕ, (m : ZMod (n i)) ≠ a i}

/-- The integers avoiding the first $k$ congruences $a_i \pmod{n_i}$. -/
def avoidPrefix (n : ℕ → ℕ) (a : ResidueChoice n) (k : ℕ) : Set ℤ :=
  {m | ∀ i : ℕ, i < k → (m : ZMod (n i)) ≠ a i}

/--
Let $n_1<n_2<\cdots$ be an infinite sequence such that, for any choice of congruence classes
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$, the set of integers not satisfying any of the congruences $a_i\pmod{n_i}$ has
density $0$. Is it true that for every $\epsilon>0$ there exists some $k$ such that, for every
choice of congruence classes $a_i$, the density of integers not satisfying any of the congruences
$a_i\pmod{n_i}$ for $1\leq i\leq k$ is less than $\epsilon$?

The answer is yes; the linked Lean proof formalizes Somani's argument.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos281.lean"]
theorem erdos_281 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ → ℕ), StrictMono n → (∀ i, 0 < n i) →
      (∀ a : ResidueChoice n, Set.HasIntDensity (avoidAll n a) 0) →
        ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
          ∃ k : ℕ, ∀ a : ResidueChoice n,
            ∃ d : ℝ, Set.HasIntDensity (avoidPrefix n a k) d ∧ d < ε := by
  sorry

end Erdos281

reformulations.difference: Lean explicitly uses two-sided natural density on ℤ, counting in [-N,N], rather than the usual one-sided positive-integer density convention.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Write A(a) for the integers avoiding the chosen residues. Reflection gives -m ∈ A(a) iff m ∈ A(-a). Therefore the symmetric count for A(a) equals its positive-side count plus the positive-side count for A(-a), with at most one additional point at zero. Since the hypothesis quantifies over every residue choice, one-sided density zero for every choice implies two-sided density zero for every choice. Conversely, symmetric density zero implies one-sided density zero by nonnegativity and comparison of the counts. For the conclusion, every finite-prefix avoidance set is periodic with positive period lcm(n(0), …, n(k−1)); both density conventions consequently exist and equal the proportion of allowed residues in one period. The universal zero-density hypothesis equivalence and positive periodicity were proved in Lean; the full density-convention reformulation was not formalized end to end.

review.notes: All four declarations were checked. Lean experiments in /workspace/review/ verified boundary cases, satisfiability of the hypotheses, inhabited residue choices, congruence semantics, extension of finite choices, density uniqueness/nonnegativity, and finite-prefix periodicity. The linked proof’s statement was checked to be definitionally equivalent to the theorem’s right-hand side. Its source contains no sorry or custom axioms, but its original Lean/Mathlib v4.29.1 build was not reproduced; the local toolchain is v4.33.1. Halberstam–Roth §V.3 was access-restricted, so only the available chapter preview and bibliography were read. This did not prevent settling any declaration against the original Erdős–Graham statement and the current problem page.
